title: Initial resistance to Company regulation
detail: Banglapedia places the beginning of the resistance in 1760, when Company regulations on alms and revenue disturbed the mendicant communities that relied on pilgrimage routes and patronage.

title: Attacks on Company establishments
detail: The revolt gathered momentum as rebels struck Company kuthi and revenue offices in Dhaka, Bakerganj, and Rampur Boalia, signalling an organised challenge to Company presence.

title: Famine intensifies the conflict
detail: The Bengal famine of 1770 deepened social distress and widened rebel support, making the resistance part of the wider crisis of early Company rule.

title: Late crackdown and gradual decline
detail: The final phase came with tighter Company administration and the weakening of rebel leadership, after which the movement gradually faded.
